## Appearance

Owen Ford is a tall, broad-shouldered man with thick brown hair. He possesses a finely-cut nose and chin, complemented by large, brilliant dark-gray eyes.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008)_

## Personality

Owen Ford is a man in his early to mid-thirties who possesses a pleasant voice, a delightful smile, and a good sense of dress. He is currently contemplating writing a novel.

## History

Owen Ford was a magazine writer and newspaper man who was ordered to the sea by his doctor to recover from a bad spell of typhoid. As the grandson of schoolmaster [John Selwyn](../character/john-selwyn.md), he arrived at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) to board with [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) and aspired to write a great Canadian novel. Upon meeting Captain Jim, Owen became enthralled by the old sailor's memories and spent the summer writing a book based on Captain Jim's life-book. During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), but left the harbor in agony due to her marriage to [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md). He later returned after learning [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) was free, confessed his love to her in the garden, and sealed their commitment. Shortly after, Owen had his manuscript published and presented as a completed book to Captain Jim.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P1](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P2](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P4](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0004), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P6](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0006), +247 more_

## Quotes

> "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)

> “We’ll collaborate,” cried Owen delightedly. “You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.”
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)

> “I have a good deal to do to it yet—revising and pruning and so forth,” he said, “but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall.”
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P19](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0019)

> "Yes,—he’s mentally deficient, or something of the sort, isn’t he? But she said nothing about Mrs. Moore, and I supposed she’d be the usual hustling country housewife who takes in boarders to earn an honest penny."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P30](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0030)

> "Oh, I won’t mind him. I don’t suppose I’ll be much in the house anyhow, except for meals. But what a shame it all is! Her life must be a hard one."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P32](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0032)

## Relationships

### [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/leslie-moore--owen-ford.md)

Owen Ford first meets [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) when he arrives at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) to board at her house, where he is immediately struck by her beauty. Over the course of a memorable summer, the two spend extensive leisure time together alongside their mutual friends, developing a mutual love and romantic connection. Although [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) initially distresses over what she believes to be unrequited feelings, their bond deepens, and the community anticipates their potential match following revelations regarding Leslie's freedom.

- Romantically involved with — mutual love and courtship  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 26 OWEN FORD’S CONFESSION P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 28 ODDS AND ENDS P24](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0024), [v4 CHAPTER 32 MISS CORNELIA DISCUSSES THE AFFAIR P18](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0018), +3 more</sub>

### [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--uncle-jim.md)

Owen meets Captain Jim after [Anne](../character/anne.md) introduces him to the lighthouse keeper, who shares his captivating life-book and sea tales. Deeply impressed by these stories, Owen becomes a close friend and collaborator, setting up a workspace at the lighthouse to write Captain Jim's life story alongside the tale of lost [Margaret](../character/margaret.md). They spend the summer working intensely together until the manuscript is finished and accepted for publication.

- Comrade of — collaborators on the book  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 39 CAPTAIN JIM CROSSES THE BAR P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)</sub>
